The Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences endeavors to train all AVS and AHS majors, and minors to understand and critically evaluate food animal and companion animal production, nutrition, health, and physiology. The department is deeply rooted in Cal Poly Pomona’s polytechnic “become by doing” tradition, blending biological science with real-world animal husbandry. Students work across 330 acres of rangeland, 100 acres of irrigated pasture, and specialized labs for meat, wool, and production - including exposure to cattle, sheep, goats, swine, and Arabian horses. The curriculum includes pathways for pre-veterinary preparation, general animal science, and a separate animal health science program, reflecting the department’s comprehensive approach. Faculty engage in applied research and industry partnerships, advancing areas like nutrition, breeding, physiology, and biotechnology. Students enjoy a wide range of hands-on resources: teaching farms, nutrition and anatomy labs, the Arabian Horse Center, and externships such as the Santa Anita racetrack equine internship. Student groups like Pre-Vet and Livestock Club facilitate leadership, networking, and scholarship opportunities, while field placements with producers, USDA facilities, or veterinary clinics enable graduates to launch careers across veterinary, agricultural, biotech, and public health fields. courses.title: Orientation and Careers in Animal Health Science
courses.description: Outline of the academic path that students will follow. Discuss the various employment opportunities available for students graduating with this degree. courses.description: General concepts of restraint and handling of wild and domestic animals. Emphasis is on physical, chemical and moral/psychological restraint. Discussion of the tools/equipment of restraint, rope work and medical problems that might occur during restraint. Corequisite(s): AHS 1129L .

courses.title: Dentistry Skills Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to the theories, practices, and techniques of small animal dentistry. Study of common oral diseases, routine and advanced dentistry procedures, and the role of the veterinary technician in dental care. Practical knowledge of general dentistry skills within the scope of a veterinary technician license. Product fee required. Corequisite(s): AHS 3263 and AHS 3263L .
courses.prerequisites: AHS 3235 , AHS 3235L , AHS 2202 , AHS 2202L , AHS 1129 , and AHS 1129L .

courses.title: Laboratory Procedures and Clinical Pathology
courses.description: An advanced course providing instruction in hematology, clinical pathology, microbiology, and urinalysis used to diagnose health problems in veterinary clinics and diagnostic laboratories. Per university policy, students must receive a C- (1.7) or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Per university policy, students must receive a C- (1.7) or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 3235L .

courses.title: Laboratory Procedures and Clinical Pathology Laboratory
courses.description: An advanced laboratory course providing instruction in hematology, clinical pathology, microbiology, urinalysis and necropsy procedures used to diagnose health problems in veterinary clinics and diagnostic laboratories. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 3235 .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, BIO 1150 , BIO 1150L , CHM 1210 , AHS 2202 , and AHS 2202L .

courses.title: Companion Animal Nursing and Surgical Skills
courses.description: Instruction on the nursing and surgical skills required to work with companion animals, mainly dogs and cats. How to safely restrain animals, how to use anesthetic and surgical equipment, and how to use proper aseptic technique. Preparation for common surgical procedures. Students must receive a C- or better to advance through the AHS program. Corequisite(s): AHS 3263L .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, AHS 1129 / AHS 1129L , AHS 2202 / AHS 2202L , and AHS 3235 / AHS 3235L .

courses.title: Surgical Nursing Skills Laboratory
courses.description: Gain experience in the skills required to work in the veterinary surgical arena. Learn the different types of anesthetics used, surgical equipment, instruments and aseptic technique. Familiarize with the preparation for common surgical procedures. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 3263 .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, AHS 3235 / AHS 3235L , AHS 2202 / AHS 2202L , and AHS 2208 / AHS 2208L .

courses.title: Parasitology and Infectious Diseases
courses.description: Animal parasites and pathogens and their relationship to clinical and subclinical parasitic diseases, as well as common diseases and disease processes of livestock, companion animals, laboratory animals and wildlife. Per university policy, students must receive a C- (1.7) or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 3305L .
courses.prerequisites: AHS major, AVS major, AG Science major, AG 1010 , or instructor permission; BIO 1150 or BIO 1210 ; and BIO 1150L or BIO 1210L .

courses.description: Study of animal parasites and pathogens and their relationship to clinical and subclinical parasitic diseases, as well as common diseases and disease processes of livestock, companion animals, laboratory animals and wildlife. courses.description: The use of clinical chemical procedures, the classification and action of pharmaceuticals, and the dispensing of medications will be studied. Includes conversion and calculation of drugs, prescription writing and routes of administration. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Per university policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 3307L .

courses.description: Instruction in laboratory and exotic animal medicine including husbandry, biological data, common diseases and conditions, research policy and procedures, and animal welfare. Corequisite(s): AHS 3369L .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, AHS 104 or AHS 1104 , AHS 129 or AHS 1129 , AHS 129L or AHS 1129L , and junior or senior standing.

courses.description: Instruction on handling and restraint, identification, and common procedures of laboratory and exotic animals. Instruction includes concepts of laboratory animal facility management, personnel, quality assurance, animal welfare and husbandry. Emphasis is placed on the role of the veterinary technician. Corequisite(s): AHS 3369 .

Advanced nursing and diagnostic techniques, response to disease, management of hospitalized patients, common diseases and conditions, and preventative medicine programs. Emphasis will be on the role of the veterinary technician in the veterinary hospital. Corequisite(s): AHS 4200L .
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, AHS 3263 , AHS 3263L , AHS 3307 and AHS 3307L .

courses.title: Large Animal Medicine and Nursing Skills Laboratory
courses.description: Instruction in large animal medicine and nursing skills. Hands-on experience with large animal species, including advanced handling and restraint, venipuncture, diagnostic testing and nursing care. Emphasis will be on the role of the veterinary technician in the veterinary hospital. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, AHS 3263 / AHS 3263L and AHS 3307 / AHS 3307L .

courses.title: Small Animal Medicine
courses.description: Instruction on small animal medicine. Advanced nursing and diagnostic techniques, response to disease, management of hospitalized patients, common diseases and conditions, intensive care, toxicology and preventative medicine programs. Emphasis will be on the role of the veterinary technician in the veterinary hospital.
courses.prerequisites: AHS 3235 , AHS 3235L , AHS 3263 , AHS 3263L , AHS 3307 , AHS 3307L , AHS 4407 , and AHS 4407L .

Per department policy, students must receive a C- or better in this course to advance in the Animal Health Science program. Corequisite(s): AHS 4407L and AHS 4408L .

courses.title: Surgical Recovery, Nursing and Critical Care Laboratory
courses.description: Instruction in the specific concepts of intensive care, recovery and veterinary nursing of surgical and anesthetic patients. Corequisite(s): Animal Health Science major, AHS 4407 , and AHS 4407L .

courses.title: Clinical Internship II
courses.description: Practical experience working in public or private clinics or laboratories where application of animal health sciences or research takes place. Experiences should be useful in preparation for state board exams in veterinary technology and/or AAALAC exams for certification in laboratory animal care. This course is intended for lower division students in the Animal Health Sciences major.

Experiences should be useful in preparation for state board exams in veterinary technology and/or AAALAC exams for certification in laboratory animal care. This course is intended for lower division students in the Animal Health Sciences major. May be taken up to two times for a total credit of 2 units.

courses.title: Veterinary Economics and Office Procedures
courses.description: Principles of veterinary economics and office procedures as they relate to companion animals. This will include medical record-keeping, navigation of practice management software, inventory and economic analysis, and electronic medical records. Client communication, team building and managing stress within a high stakes environment will be explored in depth. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, junior or senior standing, and AHS 2210 .

courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: Synthesis of disease processes, including medical, pharmacological and nursing aspects of the disease. Preparation for the Veterinary Technician National Exam. Review of the Veterinary Practice Act with emphasis on veterinary technician scope of practice. Veterinary technician licensure, legal and continuing education requirements for licensure. Continued study of client communication, interpersonal skills, and veterinary professional mental health. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: Animal Health Science major, senior standing, AHS 4407 , and AHS 4407L .

courses.title: Orientation to Animal and Veterinary Sciences
courses.description: Outlining the academic path that students will follow to be successful in this major. Discuss the various employment opportunities available for students graduating with this degree. Covering campus life, university rules, policies and regulations. Mandatory fall quarter course for entering freshmen. Strategies to assist students with the transition from school to university and the successful completion of their college career in the Animal & Veterinary Science department. Topics covered include: campus student support services, career planning, time management, academic planning, study/note/test skills, learning styles, navigating the college and university, professional development, extracurricular activities, and others.
courses.prerequisites: AVS major.

courses.title: Food Animal Production
courses.description: A study of the domestic livestock industry and animal management techniques emphasizing the importance of management strategies, equipment and facilities, nutrition, selection, breeding principles and disease control to ensure scientifically based management decisions.
courses.prerequisites: AVS major.

courses.title: Companion, Laboratory and Exotic Animal Care
courses.description: General concepts of handling and restraining domestic and exotic animals. Emphasis will be placed on behavior, management, nutrition, disease prevention, and breed identification. The care and use of laboratory animals will be covered in depth.
courses.prerequisites: AVS major.

courses.title: Food Animal Production Laboratory
courses.description: A study of the commonly applied animal techniques and practices used to scientifically manage livestock in the commercial food animal industry. The laboratory will emphasize the importance of evaluating business management strategies, equipment and facilities, nutrition, genetics and selection, breeding principles and herd health plans in order of evaluate scientifically based domestic animal livestock management methodologies. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: AVS major.

courses.title: Companion Animal Management Laboratory
courses.description: Instruction will cover the general concepts of handling and restraining domestic and exotic animals. Emphasis will be placed on behavior, management, nutrition, disease prevention, and breed identification. The care and use of laboratory animals will be covered in depth. Product fee required.
courses.prerequisites: AVS major.

courses.title: Equine Management Science
courses.description: A study of horse industry emphasizing the importance of breeds, selection, evaluation, nutrition, breeding principles, disease control, equipment, facilities to ensure scientifically based management decisions. Corequisite(s): AVS 1125L .

courses.title: Equine Management Laboratory
courses.description: A study of horse industry emphasizing the importance of breeds, selection, evaluation, nutrition, breeding principles, disease control, equipment, facilities to ensure scientifically based management decisions. Corequisite(s): AVS 1125 .

courses.title: Medical Terminology
courses.description: Introduction to medical terminology with specific application for veterinary science. Medical terminology is a universal language used in all aspects of the medical/health/research community. Designed to familiarize the student in such language by providing a basic understanding of word roots, prefixes, suffixes and abbreviations used in the field, preparing them for situations in which they will be communicating with others in the medical/veterinary field.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Animal Nutrition
courses.description: A comprehensive introduction to animal nutrition with an emphasis on nutrients, digestive physiology, digestion, and feedstuff characteristics. Focus on developing a foundation for understanding more advanced topics in nutrition including the interaction between health and nutrition. Corequisite(s): AVS 2101L .
courses.prerequisites: AVS 1112 ; CHM 1210 ; CHM 1210L ; MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , or MAT 1140 ; and AVS major.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Animal Nutrition Laboratory
courses.description: A comprehensive and applied introduction to animal nutrition with an emphasis on nutrients, digestive physiology, digestion, feed ingredient characteristics, feed identification, and ration formulation. Includes practical activities focused on developing the understanding necessary to balance appropriate diets. Corequisite(s): AVS 2101 .
courses.prerequisites: AVS major; AVS 1112 ; CHM 1210 ; CHM 1210L ; and MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , or MAT 1140 .

courses.title: Drugs and Society
courses.description: Identification and explanation of the action of different drugs. The compounds discussed include over-the-counter drugs, prescription drugs, social drugs, and drugs of abuse. How addictions develop, why they are harmful, and how to stop them. Emphasizes human pharmacology although the principles are the same for animals.

courses.title: Foal Watch
courses.description: Basic equine breeding management, care of the pregnant mare, methods to detect impending foaling and parturition, difficulties that might occur during foaling, post foaling care and potential problems/disorder in foals.

courses.title: Animal Practicum
courses.description: Practical hands on animal technical training. Activities including animal handling, restraint, care, health management, production and industry standards are taught through applied supervised experiences with one or more domestic animal species.

courses.title: Animal Genetics
courses.description: An introductory course dealing with the basic genetics of all species of livestock and common companion animals. Emphasis will be placed on inherited abnormalities, traits of economic importance, conventional methods of dealing with these traits, and technologies of the future.
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1150 or BIO 1210 , BIO 1150L or BIO 1210L , and AVS major.

courses.title: Animal Industry and Society
courses.description: [GE 5D] Analysis of the application of science in the food animal industry and animal production systems, the role and use of food animals and animal products in resolving problems associated with humanity, and the influence of animal agriculture on history, civilization and human values.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Meat Science
courses.description: Introduction to processing and utilization of fresh and value-added red meat products. Discussions on identity standards, factors affecting sensory, nutritional and shelf-life quality attributes, food safety (microbiological, chemical and physical hazards), including inspection and grading of red meats.

courses.title: Canine and Feline Compendium
courses.description: [GE 5D] How the origins and evolution of the domestic dog and cat influence their behavior and unique nutritional requirements, how selection for desired traits leads to breed associated problems. Emergency first aid, nutrition, calculation of caloric requirements, common diseases, vaccines and the immune system, zoonotic diseases (diseases transmitted from animals to man.)
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Anatomy and Physiology
courses.description: An integrated approach to the structure and function of animal systems. Topics to be discussed include the cell, the muscular-skeletal system, the nervous system, the cardiovascular system, the respiratory system, and the excretory system. Corequisite(s): AVS 3350L .
courses.prerequisites: BIO 1150 or BIO 1210 , BIO 1150L or BIO 1210L , CHM 1210 , CHM 1210L , and AVS major.

courses.title: Domestic Animal Anatomy Laboratory
courses.description: An integrated approach to the structure and function of animal systems. Topics to be discussed include the cell, the muscular-skeletal system, the nervous system, the cardio-vascular system, the respiratory system, and the excretory system. Corequisite(s): AVS 3350 .
courses.prerequisites: AVS major; BIO 115, BIO 1150 , BIO 121 or BIO 1210 ; BIO 115L, BIO 1150L , BIO 121L, or BIO 1210L ; CHM 121 or CHM 1210 ; and CHM 121L or CHM 1210L .

courses.title: Equine Herd Health
courses.description: A study of the etiology, clinical signs, and control of infectious, nutritional and parasitic diseases of horses. 3 Lecture Corequisite(s): AVS 3365L .
courses.prerequisites: AVS 125 or AVS 1125 ; and AVS 125L or AVS 1125L .

courses.title: Equine Herd Health Laboratory
courses.description: Application of the fundamental aspects of preventative equine herd health diseases, veterinary care, nutrition, management, animal welfare and basic equine emergencies. 3 hour Laboratory Corequisite(s): AVS 3365 .
courses.prerequisites: AVS 125 or AVS 1125 ; and AVS 125L or AVS 1125L .

courses.title: Animal Behavior
courses.description: The study of animal behavior including learning, cognition, behavioral physiology, biorhythms and social behavior. Emphasis will be placed on the behavior of domesticated species.
courses.prerequisites: AVS 1112 or AVS 112, AVS 1113 or AVS 113, AVS 1114L or AVS 114L, and AVS 1115L or AVS 115L.

courses.title: Companion Animal Behavior
courses.description: The study of companion animal behavior will include of organization of behaviors frequently exhibited by companion animals, behavioral motivators, common behavioral problems in companion animals, and behavioral intervention techniques. Emphasis will be in species most frequently selected for companionship.
courses.prerequisites: AVS 1112 , AVS 1113 , AVS 1114L , and AVS 1115L .

courses.title: Special Study for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Individual or group investigation, research, studies, or surveys of selected problems at advanced level. Proposals to be initiated by student(s) with guidance from faculty. Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times only with different topics Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.description: Laboratory, field, or computational research conducted under faculty supervision. Recommended for students contemplating graduate or professional school training. A maximum of 3 units can be applied as a program elective for AVS majors.
courses.prerequisites: Instructor consent.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 3 units.

courses.title: Mammalian Endocrinology and Physiology of Reproduction and Lactation
courses.description: Surveying the endocrine glands and their role roll in controlling development, growth, metabolism, digestion, metabolic regulation of physiological functions and the processes of reproduction from gametogenesis to parturition and galactopoiesis and lactation in domestic food producing animals. Corequisite(s): AVS 4214L .
courses.prerequisites: AVS major; AVS 350 or AVS 3350 ; and AVS 350L or AVS 3350L .

courses.title: Mammalian Reproduction and Lactational Physiology Laboratory
courses.description: A general laboratory course examining those factors which control reproductive function in domestic animals. Examine reproductive function in the female from puberty through pregnancy and parturition and from gametogenesis through puberty and gamete collection and cryopreservation in the male. 3 hour Laboratory Product fee required. Corequisite(s): AVS 4214 .
courses.prerequisites: AVS major; AVS 350 or AVS 3350 ; and AVS 350L or AVS 3350L .

courses.title: Reproductive Physiology and Management
courses.description: Provides a comprehensive study of mammalian reproductive physiology, covering humans, livestock, and companion animals. Explores the development of the reproductive system, sexual differentiation and maturation, spermatogenesis, oogenesis, and the estrus and menstrual cycles. Key topics include the cellular and hormonal regulation of fertilization, implantation, pregnancy, parturition, and lactation. An overview of relevant assisted reproductive management procedures used clinically and in the livestock industry by conclusion of course. Corequisite(s): AVS 4215L .
courses.prerequisites: AVS 3350 and AVS 3350L .

courses.title: Reproductive Physiology and Management Laboratory
courses.description: Experiential lab focusing on practical reproductive management techniques across different mammalian species. Learn estrus detection methods using both observation and specialized estrus detection tools. Learn artificial insemination techniques in livestock animals and perform pregnancy detection through ultrasound imaging, hormonal ELISA assays, and rectal palpation. Visit a local dairy to learn about the reproductive management of dairy cattle and perform colostrum quality testing. Observational field trip to either a specialized veterinary theriogenology unit, human human-assisted reproduction lab, or on-farm livestock management clinic. Corequisite(s): AVS 4215 .
courses.prerequisites: AVS 3350 and AVS 3350L . Pre or Corequisite(s):

courses.title: Mammalian Endocrinology
courses.description: A focused and thorough exploration of the endocrine system and its vital role in regulating growth, health, and development of livestock and companion animals. Systematically examine all major endocrine glands, including the thyroid, adrenal, and pituitary glands, to understand the fundamental role these glands play in supporting animal health. Apply this knowledge to clinical endocrinology, in which they discuss endocrine disorders, including hypothyroidism/hyperthyroidism, adrenal insufficiency, and Cushing’s disease. Learning is reinforced by the presentation of real-world clinical cases in small student groups. Provides a practical experience in diagnostics and therapeutic management. Preparation for veterinary, biomedical, or specialized animal science careers.
courses.prerequisites: AVS 3350 and AVS 3350L . Pre or Corequisite(s):

courses.title: Equine Exercise Physiology
courses.description: The basic and applied physiology of the exercising horse. Discussion of muscular respiratory, cardiovascular, nutritional, and osmoregulatory physiology. Includes gait analysis, lameness and pharmacology.
courses.prerequisites: AVS 350 or AVS 3350 ; and AVS 350L or AVS 3350L .

courses.title: Advanced Nutrition
courses.description: Review of the advanced concepts of nutrient digestion and absorption; metabolism of proteins, carbohydrates, fats, minerals, and vitamins. Relate those concepts to applied feeding practices used in livestock production.
courses.prerequisites: AVS 101 or AVS 2101 , and AVS 2101L .

courses.title: Internship in Animal Science
courses.description: On-the-job training in animal science, providing collegiate level experiences in animal production, agribusiness and related areas. Experiences may be useful for preparation of senior projects. Total credit limited to 16 units. Mandatory credit/no credit grading basis.
courses.prerequisites: Animal Science Major Pre or Corequisite(s): Permission of coordinator required before registering

courses.title: Biotechnology Applications in Animal Science
courses.description: A study of the principles and practical applications of biotechnology in Animal Science. Discussion of the implications of genetic engineering, gene transfer, transgenic animals, embryo transfer and embryo manipulation for livestock improvement; present and future importance to the agriculture industry; human and veterinary medicine, ethical issues, patent law and strategies for future problem-solving. Appreciation of biotechniques with relevance to the Animal Sciences. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement. Corequisite(s): AVS 4430LW .
courses.prerequisites: AVS 3305 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Senior Seminar
courses.description: New methods and developments, practices, and procedures in a variety of areas in the field of animal science.
courses.prerequisites: Senior Standing.

courses.title: Special Topics for Upper Division Students
courses.description: Group study at an advanced level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.

courses.title: Graduate Internship in Animal Science
courses.description: Individualized study, research, or professional experience related to animal science under the direction of a faculty member. May be repeated for up to a maximum of 4 units.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate students, Unconditional standing required

courses.title: Advanced Topics in Animal Physiology
courses.description: An advanced study of the physiology of domestic animals. Recent research developments in animal physiology. Topics include in-depth discussion of the nervous, endocrine, digestive, respiratory, circulatory, and excretory systems
courses.prerequisites: AVS 350 or AVS 3350 , and AVS 350L or AVS 3350L ; or equivalent.

courses.title: Animal Science Seminar
courses.description: In depth literature review, seminars and critiques addressing current topics in Animal Science.

courses.description: Group study at a graduate level of a selected well-defined topic or area not covered by a regularly offered course.

courses.description: Individual research in a specialized area, under the direction of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, and permission of instructor and department chair. Total credit limited to six units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester. courses.title: Independent Research
courses.description: Individual study/investigation and research in a specialized area proposed by the student with the approval, and under the supervision, of a graduate faculty member; work does not pertain directly to the thesis.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate standing, and permission of instructor and department chair. Pre or Corequisite(s): Graduate standing, and permission of instructor and department chair.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 6 units, with a maximum of 3 units per semester.

courses.title: Project Development
courses.description: Develop and execute an intensive independent project based on a critical need within the Animal Sciences. Work with faculty advisor to draft a comprehensive project proposal and analyze data to refine their methodology and then complete their project. Projects can be practical applications such as writing animal handling manuals, creating lab manuals, or completing a systematic literature review.
courses.prerequisites: MS in Agricultural Sciences and Technology - Animal Science option, project emphasis.
courses.repeat_for_credit: May be taken multiple times Minimum - Maximum Units: Total credit limited to 4 units.

courses.title: Master Thesis / Project Research
courses.description: Individual research in the area of specialization conducted as part of the preparation for writing a thesis under the direction of graduate faculty.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate student, Unconditional standing required.

courses.title: Project Report
courses.description: Finalize and present independent project. Requires the production of a concise, professionally written final report, approved by the faculty advisor, detailing the project’s background, consultations, methodology, and the finished product. Successful completion requires the final report submission by the Graduate Studies deadline and a public presentation of the project as the culminating experience. Typically taken during the final semester of the program. Pre or Corequisite(s): AVS 6930 .

courses.title: Master’s Degree Thesis
courses.description: Compilation, evaluation, interpretation, and report of research for thesis directed by a committee of graduate faculty members. Completion of approved, bound thesis.
courses.prerequisites: Graduate students only. Advancement to Candidacy required.
